thread:
anya_support: Customer reported sudden 502/504s hitting hosted inference during a tenant scaling job, started ~1743210000. They say streaming responses fail mid-stream and non-streamed requests sometimes return 502.

anya_support: Repro steps from customer: 1) open 8 concurrent streaming requests with payload ~1.5MB each (chunked). 2) keep connections open for ~45s. 3) ~50% fail with 502, others finish but are delayed. They provided curl sample:
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"model":"rwd-3b","input":"<big prompt>"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

anya_support: Customer also included edge trace IDs: trace=tx-8f3a, tx-8f3b, tx-8f3c (all around the same second). They think it started after they ramped tenant qps from 20->120.

leo_sre: Looking. Any deploys/flags around that time? Can we get envoy logs + edge proxy (nginx) access logs and upstream traces for tx-8f3a..c? Also curious if this correlates with dedicated "transparent compression" toggle that went live yesterday.

deploy-bot: canary/deploys:edge-compression-toggle v1.2.3 -> canary at 1743209400, rollout to 30% at 1743209600.

mike_eng: FYI I flipped the transparent compression flag to canary yesterday (reduces CPU on large bodies). Haven't seen errors in our perf tests but we didn't exercise large concurrent chunked streaming.

sam_ops: I pulled the access logs for tx-8f3a: upstream responded with "upstream prematurely closed connection" (502) and nginx showed "client aborted" in 3 of 8 requests. Also saw repeated TLS session renegotiation entries for that tenant's client IP.

leo_sre: Interesting — two signals: upstream (model-serving) closing connection early + TLS session churn. Could be compression module interacting with streaming/chunked transfer and causing a mismatch in content-length/chunk handling, leading upstream to drop.

leo_sre: Can you paste a short example of the raw request/response bytes if customer captured them? Otherwise I'll enable debug logs on edge and temporarily disable compression canary for that segment to confirm.

anya_support: Customer supplied a small tcpdump snippet (sanitized) that shows repeated FIN from upstream right after first data frame when compression header present. They asked us to repro locally with their payload.

mike_eng: I'll spin up a local edge with compression enabled + an upstream mock that accepts chunked streaming. Repro plan: replay their 8 concurrent chunked payloads at similar pacing. If I can reproduce, I'll run with and without compression.

sam_ops: In the meantime I patched an nginx route to set proxy_buffering off for that tenant's path and temporarily removed them from the compression canary. Could mitigate while we validate.

anya_support: Customer confirmed a partial improvement after we pulled them from canary — success rate improved to ~90% (from ~50%). They still see occasional 502 but much better. :thumbsup:

leo_sre: Good signal. Next steps: (1) mike to reproduce and create minimal test case, (2) eng + sres to audit compression + chunked streaming code path in edge (especially handling of chunk size metadata and early-flush), (3) ops to keep tenant out of canary until fix.

mike_eng: On it. If I can't repro, I'll request packet captures and exact request timings from customer. Leaving a small debug toggle on the canary to capture full request/response stacks for the affected tenant only.

anya_support: I'll keep customer updated and escalate SLA if they want an emergency rollback. Thanks team.

customer_io: Thanks for the quick turnaround — appreciate the mitigation and happy to provide more traces if needed.

leo_sre: tagging follow-up: add an alert for "edge-compression:upstream-abort-rate" > 1% over 1m for tenant route, and a runbook note about disabling compression for chunked/streaming-heavy tenants.

anya_support: noted. Closing thread when mike posts repro or ops confirms rollback.
